paper_metadata.title: The Deformation Behaviors and Mechanism of the High-Temperature Mechanical Properties of a Ni48W35Co17 Alloy

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: Investigations of the plastic deformation mechanisms of Ni-W-based heavy alloys varying with increasing temperatures are very important for the development of hot forming processes and applications at elevated temperatures. In this study, the continuous variation of strength and plasticity of a novel Ni-W-based heavy alloy with increasing temperatures was investigated.

evidence.section: 2. Experimental Procedure
evidence.quote: Ni48W35Co17 (mass fraction, %) alloys were prepared using pure Ni, W, and Co master alloys in a magnetic suspension vacuum arc-melting furnace under a vacuum degree of 104 Pa. Air cooling treatment was used after melting, and the temperature decreased by 3–5 ◦C every 2 s. Then, the as-cast alloys were forged two times at approximately 1200 ◦C, and ﬁnally, Ni48W35Co17 bars with a 20 mm diameter were obtained.

evidence.section: 2. Experimental Procedure
evidence.quote: The investigation of the precipitation process of the high-temperature mechanical properties was conducted using a Gleeble8100 thermal deformation simulation testing machine (DSI, Minnesota St. Paul, MN, USA). In a quasi-static tensile test, the strain rate was 5 × 10−4 s−1. The tests were repeated for three times under each condition, to minimize the experimental errors.
